title: The Kitchen Sink Mistake Ruining Your Pipes
description: Pouring used cooking oil or palm oil down your kitchen sink is one of the most common causes of stubborn drainage blockages. While oil looks completely liquid when warm in your frying pan, it cools down rapidly once it meets the standing water inside your under-sink P-trap. As the oil cools, it congeals onto the inner walls of the PVC waste pipe, trapping fine food debris and gradually narrowing the drainage passage. Over time, this forms a hard grease plug that completely stops water flow. Always allow cooking fat to cool, collect it in a waste container, and wipe greasy pans with paper towels before washing.

visual_story: The viewer sees the inside of a kitchen sink cabinet where a white plastic P-trap has been opened for maintenance. The first detail the viewer notices is the thick, hardened layer of congealed oil sitting inside the pipe curve. This visual detail proves that liquid oil poured down a sink does not stay fluid, but solidifies inside cool drainage components, choking water flow.
